earlier_scan.source_named: Meng, Chaoji. 2001. Yaozu Bunuyu Fangyan Yanjiu [A Study of the Bunu Dialects of the Yao People]. Beijing: Minzu Chubanshe (covers Numao)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page numa1251 'Numao' (alt. name Nu-hmou); refs Meng 2001:149-192, Niederer 2002:216, Ratliff 2010.
sources.note: Bibliographic/classificatory only; zero descriptive references attached to numa1251 itself.

Nothing on stress; give autonyms nu22 m̥ou11 (Numao, ~1,200 speakers, Yaolu and Jiarong townships) and toŋ11 m̥uŋ11 (Dongmeng, ~400 speakers, Maolan/Dongtang/Weng'ang), 1,715 speakers (2001), citing Meng 2001, Zhou Guoyan 2013 and Guizhou sheng zhi: Minzu zhi 2002.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien Language History. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: The Australian National University. (Open Access, CC BY-SA, hdl 1885/146760)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Numao/Yaolu data at all (its Bunu data points are Qibainong Bunu = Dongnu and 'Yaoli Bunu' = Nao Klao of Nandan, Wang & Mao 1995 #10/#11, plus Meizhu Bunu from Niederer). Only a family-level prosody remark, p.28, quoting Downer 1961 on Mien: reduced syllables have 'weaker stress and shorter duration than the following full syllables so that a strong iambic rhythm is imparted to disyllabic words' -- about Mienic vowel-length languages, not Bunu/Numao. Nothing on word stress in Numao.

sources.citation: Strecker, David. 1987. The Hmong-Mien languages. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 10(2): 1-11.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Classification paper; p.3 lists '16. Pu-Nao subgroup (Bunuyu Bu-Nao fangyan).. e. Nu Mhou (Bunuyu Numao tuyu)' -- confirms identity of Numao as a Bunu (Pu-Nao) variety; no prosodic information.
